newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat opposition drops parliament boycott.
newsitem.headline: Croat opposition drops parliament boycott.

text.p: The Croatian opposition dropped its boycott of the country's parliament on Wednesday after the assembly agreed to discuss disputed Zagreb city elections.
Croatian TV showed opposition members sitting in parliament and beginning debate on the country's 1997 budget.
Oppositon MPs walked out of parliament last week and threatened a one-month boycott after failing to have their proposal for an end to the "Zagreb crisis" put on the agenda.

The opposition won a clear victory in municipal elections in Zagreb but the ruling HDZ, led by hardline President Franjo Tudjman, would not accept the victory and for more than a year has refused to accept a non-HDZ mayor.

The parliament was due to discuss a proposed budget increase of some 10 percent to 39.4 billion kuna ($7.29 billion) to meet higher spending needs and repay almost four billion kuna public debt next year.
But the government said the deficit would remain under three percent as it hoped to cover most current expenditures by tax and other revenues.
The upper chamber of the parliament (Sabor) approved budget plans on Tuesday. ($=5.403)
